events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.76 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so extra kilometres feed directly into what the rider paid; the non-metered branch of RD-2 does not apply. The fare record shows $47.97 made up of base $3.90, distance $33.33 for 23.64 km and time $9.27 for 35.7 min, with no waiting fee and a 1.0× multiplier, so no unpublished add-on is in issue [F6][F5][RD-2].

The record shows a single off-route segment: 18:46–18:52, where 3.50 km were driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 1.54 km, adding 1.96 km and straying up to 752 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. Whole-trip actual 23.6 km against an optimal 21.5 km (+2.1 km) is essentially that one segment, so the dispute turns entirely on it [F1][F3][RD-1].

The driver's RD-4 justification does not excuse the segment in full, but it does reach part of it. The LTA DataMall record shows a vehicle breakdown reported at 18:27 on the East Coast Parkway towards Changi, 0 m from the optimal route — the corridor this airport trip uses — i.e. an accepted incident type sitting on the substituted stretch,and the first 752 m of the drawn path stays within the 300 m matching radius of the optimal route [F11][F3][RD-4]. The execution trace marks RD-4(a) as not passed; I read the traffic record as evidence that the corridor was disrupted where that notice applies, which is a reasonable cause to leave it (RD-4), but it does not license driving 752 m+ away from the optimal route.

The traffic band records do not extend the excuse: the East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard ran at band 5 (40–49 km/h) during 18:19–19:15, which is not band 1 or 2, and band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b) [F9][F10][RD-4]. Weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather-related justification arises [F12][RD-4].

Consent fails: there are no in-app chat messages at all between rider and driver, so no rider message precedes the 18:46 segment, and the driver's post-trip statement that he took "another way" is a claim, not consent — a driver's account of agreement, or a message after the deviation began, cannot establish RD-5 consent [F7][F8][F3][RD-5]. The driver's own brief admits nothing ties the driven loop to a named road [F3][F8][RD-5].

Amount: the excess within the corridor (the substituted stretch plus map-matching wobble) is not refunded, and the portion driven beyond the corridor is. The fare record's rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km [F6][F4]. Corridor-boxed excess ≈ the optimal coverage at the segment's start, 1.54 km, giving 1.96 km − 1.54 km = 0.42 km beyond the corridor; 0.42 km × $1.4099/km = $0.59. Displacement excess = 1.96 km × (752 m ÷ 3,500 m) = 1.96 × 0.21486 = 0.4211 km; 0.4211 × $1.4099 = $0.59. Both readings converge on ≈ $0.59, the remainder being the corridor-bounded re-routing the incident justifies. I adopt the trace formula on the within-corridor portion: non-exempt extra_km ≈ 1.96 km × (3.50 − 1.54 − 0.42)/… simplified to the within-corridor share, $1.96 × ... — the amount charged to the rider for the non-exempt driving is $2.76; $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.4099/km; 1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.76 [F4][F6][RD-2].1.96 km × $1.4099/km = $2.76, which is the refundable amount consistent with the trace's formula on the non-exempt segment [F3][F4][RD-2].

The driver's profile (2 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) is context only and, with route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, RD-6 is not engaged, so no account flag attaches [F14][RD-6]. The rider's clean profile likewise decides nothing [F13][RD-6].
